look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST — PRAIRIE TEA: A low, repeatedly branching annual Croton with small, entire-edged leaves, pale stellate-hairy underside, and tiny clustered flowers. THE DECISIVE MICRO-CLUES are (A) abaxial dark-BROWN-CENTERED stellate hairs that look like little brown dots with a lens and (B) two female styles, each bifid, giving FOUR terminal style arms. The unusual fruit has one functional seed. Croton lindheimerianus can have nearly the same low branching habit, but its leaf underside lacks the brown-centered hair effect and it has THREE bifid styles / SIX terminal arms. Do NOT claim the exact hairs or style count can be seen in these present whole-plant photos; photograph multiple undersides and an open female flower with a scale.

morphology_keys.comparison_training: LOOK HERE FIRST: on a sharp underside macro, dark-centered stellate hairs can appear as brown specks; check multiple leaves. On a flowering female plant, count two deeply divided styles producing four terminal branches, and inspect mature fruit for the characteristically reduced one-seeded condition. Croton lindheimerianus has different leaf indumentum and typically three styles divided into six tips; C. texensis generally has narrow foliage and separate male/female plants with warty fruit. Do not identify from low bushy habit or pale flowers alone.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.title: Prairie tea: low bush first, then hairs and four tips

steps.look: Small entire leaves on widely branched low annual
steps.what: Use whole-plant photos to recognize it; near-ground branches and small clusters visible. Habit overlaps three-seed croton.

Use 10–20× lens or stacked smartphone macro of the BACK of several leaves. Brown-dot centers should be actual stellate hair disks, not dirt, fungal spots or green tissue flecks. NOT photo-proven here.

steps.look: Two BIFID styles with FOUR terminal ends
steps.what: Locate pistillate flower/early fruit; focus from above/oblique and count four endpoints. A male stamen cluster is not countable female style evidence. NOT photo-proven here.
Photograph mature fruit and seeds with millimeter ruler, show the one fertile locule if dissecting. Not shown by existing gallery.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.memory_rule: SMALL BUSH + BROWN-DOTTED STAR HAIRS + FOUR FEMALE STYLE TIPS = PRAIRIE TEA.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Croton monanthogynus: see the habit, then check underside
steps: Locate a small many-branched annual with alternating simple entire leaves.
Flip a leaf: seek actual BROWN-CENTERED star hairs at 10–20×. Current images do NOT resolve those centers.
Find a female flower and count FOUR style tips (two bifid styles); a male white staminate flower cannot prove it.
Compare with C. lindheimerianus: overlapping habit but lacking the brown-dot hair character and with SIX female tips.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Habit is provisional. Brown-centered hairs and female four tips should confirm when measurable; otherwise record Croton sp.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: The three real images show low habit/leaf/flower clusters only. Brown-centered hairs and style counts are scientifically documented but NOT visually demonstrated.
